producer_report.summary: Most of the rework was already in the base commit: the Athena title and heading, opening paragraphs, Next steps section, GitHub source links, the plain-language f2 text, and the docs, CHANGELOG and README entries. I only closed the remaining gaps. First, the captain glossary entry in intro.json now says the captain directs firstmate's AI workers and approves merges when yolo is off. It also says the study establishes the role, not who fills it. Second, I added five named tests to xtask/src/site.rs for the opening, the who-uses and captain text, the next-step links, the source links with escaped link text, and the absence of the f2 jargon. I did not touch validation.json, findings.json, or the docs. The docs already describe this behaviour and the validator did not need changes.

criteria_check.criterion: In xtask/src/site.rs the page title and first heading name Athena, and an opening paragraph says what Athena is, that the page is an example of what its study capability produces, and that firstmate is the system studied. A named test asserts this.
criteria_check.evidence: Test the_opening_says_what_athena_is_that_this_is_an_example_study_and_what_was_studied asserts the title, the h1 and the header text. The header has Athena is an open-source system, A study is Athena's written reading, and This page is that study of firstmate. Test the_page_names_athena_before_firstmate_and_has_next_steps also passes.

criteria_check.criterion: The 'What firstmate is' text says who uses firstmate and that its workers are AI coding agents. The captain glossary entry says plainly who the captain is, or what the study does and does not establish, and is not only 'The text says no more about who the captain is.'
criteria_check.evidence: Test the_real_study_says_who_uses_firstmate_and_who_the_captain_is asserts 'people who direct AI coding agents', 'a worker, which is itself an AI coding agent', 'The study establishes this role only', and the absence of the old captain sentence.

criteria_check.criterion: The page has a visible next-step section with anchor links to the Athena repository and firstmate's repository. Each claim source renders as an anchor to its file at the pinned commit, with link text HTML-escaped. Named tests cover the next-step links, the source links and the escaping.
criteria_check.evidence: Tests the_next_steps_link_to_athena_and_to_the_studied_repository, each_claim_source_is_a_link_to_its_file_at_the_pinned_commit_with_escaped_text and a_github_pin_gives_linked_repository_and_sources_and_others_do_not all pass. The escaping test checks the anchor URL and code text with <, & and quotes escaped.

criteria_check.criterion: The text for finding f2 in 'Limits of this study' no longer contains 'guard_evaluated_by for nobody' and is in plain language. A test asserts the phrase is absent from the rendered HTML.
criteria_check.evidence: Test the_f2_limit_is_in_plain_language_without_the_data_format_jargon asserts the phrase is absent and 'Some transitions have no guard' is present. findings.json f2 detail reads as plain prose.

open_issues: The deliverables list includes README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/explainer-site.md, findings.json and validation.json. I left them unchanged because they already match the page and the validator passes. I did not confirm the CHANGELOG mentions the captain wording.
mistakes: My first cargo test --locked run produced output too large to inspect, so I re-ran it with --quiet to read the results.
learnings: The base commit already contained most of the requested rework: Athena heading, Next steps, source links, f2 text and the docs and CHANGELOG entries.
CARGO_TARGET_DIR is set outside the work tree, so the site builds there rather than into target/site in the tree.
Bash output files persisted under ~/.claude are blocked from Read and Grep by the working-directory hook.
desires: A way to read persisted large tool output inside the working directory.
